claims.text: In-situ TEM can elucidate oxidation mechanisms and nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA has a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
The proposed in-situ TEM observations are conducted at 500–1000 °C with a temperature tolerance of ±10 °C.
The proposed atmosphere is air or an oxygen-rich environment with an oxygen partial pressure of 0.1 atm.
Oxidation induces elemental redistribution in the nanoprecipitates.
Oxidation induces nanoprecipitate coarsening or dissolution.
Elemental redistribution and nanoprecipitate coarsening or dissolution promote formation of a protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale reduces oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Nanoprecipitates act as sinks for oxygen and other reactive elements.
The sink action of nanoprecipitates reduces the availability of species participating in oxidation reactions.
The proposed nanoprecipitate-mediated mechanisms decrease oxide-layer thickness.
The additively manufactured alloy will exhibit a 25% reduction in oxide-layer thickness relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
The oxide-layer thickness will decrease from a baseline value of 2.5 μm to 1.875 μm.
The magnitude of oxide-thickness reduction depends on oxygen partial pressure and temperature.
The roles of grain-boundary diffusion and dislocation density in the alloy's oxidation behavior are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The atmosphere is described as either air or oxygen-rich while also being assigned a single oxygen partial pressure of 0.1 atm. Air normally has a higher oxygen partial pressure near ambient total pressure, and 0.1 atm is not oxygen-rich relative to air, so these condition descriptions are internally inconsistent or underspecified.
